physical_interpretation: In Suzuki 2008 Tables I-III, lifetimes in candidate chiral doublet bands of 103,104Rh were measured using an inverse-kinematics RDDS variant with a 3.5 mg/cm2 Nb degrader foil instead of a stopper. This slowed recoils from v/c ~ 5.1-5.7% to 3.1-3.3% while maintaining foil transit times under 0.2 ps, avoiding the Doppler attenuation smearing that plagues classical thick-stopper DSAM below 1 ps. Our quantitative audit of the extracted transition strengths in 104Rh reveals a striking structural result: the well-known even-odd spin staggering of the B(M1)/B(E2) ratio (15.1 at 10-, 9.8 at 11-, 11.3 at 12-, 6.3 at 13-) is driven entirely by staggering in B(E2) (0.063, 0.093, 0.039, 0.067 e2b2), whereas B(M1) decreases monotonically (0.95, 0.91, 0.44, 0.42 muN2) with NO odd-even staggering! Exactly the same behavior is confirmed in 103Rh: B(E2) staggers (0.077, 0.14, 0.11 e2b2) while B(M1) decreases monotonically (2.3, 1.8, 1.2 muN2). This contradicts the textbook chiral expectation from particle-rotor models where B(M1) staggers at high spin due to left/right chiral tunneling geometry, while B(E2) is smooth. This provides a critical Day 18 benchmark demonstrating that B(M1)/B(E2) staggering alone cannot diagnose chiral geometry, and that absolute lifetime measurements separating B(M1) from B(E2) are indispensable.
